questions.q: Which service typically runs its queries over UDP?
questions.solution: A single quick query-and-reply fits **UDP** (port 53); mail, FTP and HTTPS ride on reliable TCP.

questions.q: Digital computers represent all data using —
questions.solution: A **digital** computer converts every input into **discrete binary values (0 and 1)** and computes on them. Continuous quantities are the domain of analog machines.

questions.q:
Match the app to its private-window shortcut:
A. Chrome  B. Edge  C. Firefox
questions.solution: Chrome and Edge (Chromium family) share **Ctrl+Shift+N**; only Firefox uses **Ctrl+Shift+P**.

questions.q: The fastest way to rename a worksheet is to —
options: Double-click its tab, type the new name
questions.solution: A **double-click on the sheet tab** opens the rename box (right-click, Rename also works).

questions.q:
Select the option that can substitute the given group of words.

A woman whose husband has died
questions.solution: The man who has lost his wife is a widower; the woman is a **widow**. The pair word is the planted trap.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To beat about the bush
options: to search carefully in a forest
to avoid coming to the point
questions.solution: Hunters beat *around* bushes to flush game without striking it — skirting the centre. Hence **avoiding the main topic**.
questions.shortcut: Picture: striking the edges, never the centre → dodging the point.

questions.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
questions.solution: One shape only: **better** (already comparative) — 'more better' doubles the marker. The correct part reads simply '**is better** than the last one's'.

questions.q:
Select the option that is OPPOSITE in meaning to the given idiom.

To blow hot and cold
options: to hold the same opinion firmly
questions.solution: *Blow hot and cold* = to keep changing one's mind, to be unsteady. Opposite: **to hold one opinion firmly**. 'Keep changing one's opinion' is the same meaning.
questions.shortcut: Hot then cold = changing; opposite = steady.

questions.q: An award of a **Lok Adalat** is —
options: Deemed a decree of a civil court and binding
Subject to a regular appeal on merits
Valid only if confirmed by the High Court
questions.solution: Under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, a Lok Adalat award is **deemed a civil-court decree**, final and binding on the parties; no appeal lies on the merits.

questions.q: The Tamil epic **Silappadikaram** tells the tragic story of —
questions.solution: **Silappadikaram** ('the lay of the anklet') by **Ilango Adigal** follows merchant **Kovalan** and his chaste wife **Kannagi** in Madurai; its sequel is the Buddhist *Manimekalai*.

questions.q: Which is regarded as the **oldest khayal gharana** of Hindustani music?
questions.solution: **Gwalior** gharana is the oldest of the khayal gharanas; Patiala is famous for Bade Ghulam Ali Khan.

questions.q: The green pigment essential for photosynthesis is —
questions.solution: **Chlorophyll** in the chloroplasts traps sunlight; it is the reason leaves are green.

questions.q: A shopkeeper uses a weight of 800 g for a kilogram and sells his goods 20% above the cost price. His gain per cent is:
questions.shortcut: 44% multiplies 20% and 25% — wrong, because the base changes after each cheat.

questions.q: A trader sells at cost price but gives only 800 grams per kilogram. His gain per cent is:
The area of an equilateral triangle is $25\sqrt{3}$ sq cm. Its perimeter is:
questions.solution:
$\frac{\sqrt3}{4}a^2 = 25\sqrt3 \Rightarrow a^2 = 100 \Rightarrow a = 10$ cm.

Perimeter $= 3 \times 10 = 30$ cm.
questions.shortcut: $a^2 = \frac{4K}{\sqrt3} = 100$ → $a = 10$, $P = 30$ cm. Trap: $20$ cm (side doubled, not tripled).

questions.q: From a point on the ground, the elevation of an aeroplane is $60^\circ$. If the plane is $1000$ m away along the line of sight, its height above the ground is:
questions.solution: $h = 1000\sin60^\circ = 500\sqrt3$ m.
questions.shortcut: Line of sight = hypotenuse: sin60. Trap: $1000\sqrt3$ (used tan60 on the hypotenuse).

questions.q:
Three of the following four letter-clusters are alike in a certain way and one is different. Find the odd one out. (The letters follow English alphabetical order.)

**OPQR, UVWX, ABCD, STUV**
questions.solution: All four are four consecutive letters and each contains exactly one vowel. In OPQR, UVWX and ABCD the vowel is the **first** letter. In STUV the vowel U is third → **STUV**.

questions.q:
Three of the following four are alike in a certain way and one is different. Find the odd one out.

**Abundant, Plentiful, Ample, Scarce**
questions.solution: Abundant, plentiful and ample all mean **more than enough**. Scarce means **too little** → **Scarce**.

questions.q: For three sets, **|A| = 25, |B| = 30, |C| = 20, |A ∩ B| = 10, |B ∩ C| = 8, |A ∩ C| = 7** and **|A ∪ B ∪ C| = 55**. How many elements are in **all three** sets?
questions.solution: 55 = 25 + 30 + 20 − 10 − 8 − 7 + x = 50 + x → x = **5**. Check: only A = 13, only B = 17, only C = 10 — no region is negative.
questions.shortcut: Rearrange the master formula for the missing term.

questions.q: A cube of side 5 cm is painted on all its faces and then cut into 1 cm cubes. How many small cubes have **no** face painted?
questions.solution: Strip one layer from every side: the unpainted core is (5 − 2)³ = 3³ = **27**.
